about: What a data directory's layout.json says, read by the runtime's LayoutStamp (DesktopLayoutStampsTests in dotnet/tests/Jason.Cli.Tests) and by the desktop's paths.ts (test/data-layout.test.ts) from the same cases, so the two readers cannot part. A case is the file's text, its bytes in base64, or what is on disk at the name. A refusal is its code, said in that code's sentence with the case's writer, problem and stamp path, for a jason of the version current names. desktop_problem is what the desktop says where it cannot say what the runtime says: the line and byte the runtime's JSON reader stopped at. only keeps a case to the systems that can make it: posix to macOS and Linux, posix_unprivileged to those when not run as root.

sentences.layout_newer: This data directory was set up by Jason {written_by}, newer than this jason ({current}): update this jason, or use the one that set it up.
sentences.layout_unreadable: This data directory's layout stamp at {path} cannot be read ({problem}), so this jason cannot tell how the directory is laid out: use the Jason that set it up, or update this jason.
